opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee he is eligible for write (up to write; admin only if role owns the system, which applies here but write was requested). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E031 (Nathaniel Young) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested write > max, so recommend read. (Note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing full-time.)
reason: The notes conflict on employment type: HR's note says full-time (which would permit write), while Security's note says contractor with basic security training (max read for contractors without advanced training; write requires advanced training; never admin). Because the security record explicitly identifies E031 as a contractor with only basic training, granting write would exceed the contractor maximum. Per policy, grant the maximum allowed: read.
